name: Working routine
description: Vasiliy finally got to work, where there is a huge amount of tasks waiting for him. Vasiliy is given a matrix consisting of n rows and m columns and q tasks. Each task is to swap two submatrices of the given matrix. For each task Vasiliy knows six integers a i , b i , c i , d i , h i , w i , where a i is the index of the row where the top-left corner of the first rectangle is located, b i is the index of its column, c i is the index of the row of the top-left corner of the second rectangle, d i is the index of its column, h i is the height of the rectangle and w i is its width. It's guaranteed that two rectangles in one query do not overlap and do not touch, that is, no cell belongs to both rectangles, and no two cells belonging to different rectangles share a side . However, rectangles are allowed to share an angle. Vasiliy wants to know how the matrix will look like after all tasks are performed.
input_specification: The first line of the input contains three integers n , m and q ( 2 ≤ n , m ≤ 1000 , 1 ≤ q ≤ 10 000 ) — the number of rows and columns in matrix, and the number of tasks Vasiliy has to perform. Then follow n lines containing m integers v i , j ( 1 ≤ v i , j ≤ 10 9 ) each — initial values of the cells of the matrix. Each of the following q lines contains six integers a i , b i , c i , d i , h i , w i ( 1 ≤ a i , c i , h i ≤ n , 1 ≤ b i , d i , w i ≤ m ).
output_specification: Print n lines containing m integers each — the resulting matrix.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 706E — Working routine [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
